parsed_output.analysis: The model diverges from the specification in several structural and semantic ways. The initial transition, the trigger for entering autonomous mode, the internal sub-states of autonomous mode, the transition back to human driving mode, and the final/power-off handling all show discrepancies against the specification's stated behavior.

issues.issue: Initial transition goes to HumanDriving, but per spec the system should start there only implicitly via power-on; the model instead treats HumanDriving as the default initial state directly from [*], without an explicit 'Power On' event triggering entry from the initial pseudostate.
issues.reason: Spec item 3 states 'when power on, the system turns into human driving mode', implying the transition from the initial state should be labeled/triggered by 'Power On', but the model's initial transition has no such condition, while a separate 'Power On' transition is (incorrectly) used later to go from HumanDriving to Autonomous.

issues.issue: The transition from HumanDriving to Autonomous is labeled 'Power On', but according to the spec, entry into autonomous mode should be triggered by 'front_distance > 10', not by powering on.
issues.reason: Spec item 4 says 'when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state'. The model incorrectly uses 'Power On' as the trigger instead of the front distance condition, and also duplicates a nearly identical transition (HumanDriving --> Autonomous : Front Distance > 10) elsewhere, creating a conflicting/redundant guard for the same transition target.

issues.issue: Duplicate/conflicting transitions from HumanDriving to Autonomous: one triggered by 'Power On' and another by 'Front Distance > 10'.
issues.reason: The specification only defines a single triggering condition (front_distance > 10) for transitioning from human driving to autonomous mode. Having two separate transitions with different triggers to the same target state is inconsistent with the spec and introduces ambiguity about when power-on actually applies.
issues.where: HumanDriving --> Autonomous : Power On  AND  HumanDriving --> Autonomous : Front Distance > 10

issues.issue: The internal structure of the Autonomous submachine state (AutonomousIdle, AutonomousActive) is invented and not specified, and the transition logic between them (Front Distance <= 10 to go idle, Front Distance > 10 to go active) is not part of the given specification.
issues.reason: Spec item 2 only says the autonomous mode 'has sub-states' without specifying what they are or their transition conditions. The model fabricates specific idle/active sub-states and guard conditions that are not derivable from the specification, and reuses the 'Front Distance > 10' condition in a different context than the one specified (item 4 uses this condition to go FROM human driving TO autonomous, not within the autonomous submachine).
issues.where: Autonomous --> AutonomousIdle : Front Distance <= 10 ; AutonomousIdle --> AutonomousActive : Front Distance > 10

issues.issue: Transitions from AutonomousActive to HumanDriving do not include the 'in (auto final)' condition required by the specification.
issues.reason: Spec item 4 (second instance, mislabeled as 4 again) states transition to human driving mode occurs 'when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final)', implying all three conditions (or being in the auto final sub-state) are relevant triggers. The model only implements two of the three triggers and never uses or reaches an 'auto final' sub-state within the Autonomous submachine, omitting the third specified condition entirely.
issues.where: AutonomousActive --> HumanDriving : Human Steering Cmd ; AutonomousActive --> HumanDriving : Brake Pressed

issues.issue: There is no 'auto final' sub-state modeled within the Autonomous submachine state, despite the specification explicitly referencing transit to human driving mode when 'in (auto final)'.
issues.reason: The spec explicitly calls for an internal final state of the autonomous submachine ('auto final') that triggers a transition to human driving mode when reached. The model's submachine only has AutonomousIdle and AutonomousActive states with no internal final pseudostate, so the 'in (auto final)' condition from the spec cannot be satisfied by this model.
issues.where: Autonomous submachine (AutonomousIdle, AutonomousActive) — missing an internal final state

issues.issue: The transition to the final state on power off originates from HumanDriving only, but the specification states 'when power off, it will transit to final state' without restricting this to any particular mode, implying power off should be handled globally (including from Autonomous states).
issues.reason: Spec item 5 does not limit the power-off transition to the human driving mode; logically a real system should be able to power off from any active state (including Autonomous, AutonomousIdle, AutonomousActive). The model only defines this transition from HumanDriving, meaning power-off from autonomous mode is unhandled, contradicting the general nature of the specification's item 5.

issues.issue: The final state is named 'AutonomousFinal' and labeled 'Auto Final State', which conflates the overall system's final state (per spec item 5) with the autonomous submachine's internal final state referenced in spec item 4 ('auto final').
issues.reason: The specification refers to two distinct concepts: (a) an overall system final state reached on power off (item 5), and (b) an internal final state within the autonomous submachine used as a condition for returning to human driving (item 4, 'in (auto final)'). The model uses a single state, ambiguously named and described, to represent what should be two distinct concepts, causing confusion and structurally misrepresenting the specification.

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
user_prompt:
## Natural-language specification

1 The human driving mode is represented by a simple state. 2 The autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state. 3. when power on, the system turn into human driving mode 4when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state 4. transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final) 5 when power off, it will transit to final state

## State machine model (PlantUML)

@startuml
[*] --> HumanDriving
HumanDriving : Human Driving Mode

HumanDriving --> Autonomous : Power On
Autonomous : Autonomous Mode
Autonomous : <<submachine>>

Autonomous --> AutonomousIdle : Front Distance <= 10
AutonomousIdle : Autonomous Idle Mode

AutonomousIdle --> AutonomousActive : Front Distance > 10
AutonomousActive : Autonomous Active Mode

AutonomousActive --> HumanDriving : Human Steering Cmd
AutonomousActive --> HumanDriving : Brake Pressed

HumanDriving --> Autonomous : Front Distance > 10
HumanDriving --> AutonomousFinal : Power Off

AutonomousFinal : Auto Final State
@enduml
